test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which scheme focuses on providing housing for all by 2022?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)** is the flagship mission of the **Government of India** designed to provide **Housing for All** in both urban and rural areas by the year **2022**. *Hence, option 1 is correct.*

• The scheme was officially launched on **25th June 2015** by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** to coincide with the **75th anniversary** of **India’s Independence**.

• It is implemented through two distinct verticals: **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U)**, which is managed by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**, and **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G)**, which is managed by the **Ministry of Rural Development**.

• The primary objective of **PMAY-U** was to construct **2 crore houses** for the urban poor, while **PMAY-G** aimed at providing **2.95 crore pucca houses** with basic amenities to those living in kutcha houses or dilapidated houses in rural areas.

• The mission ensures **women empowerment** by mandating that the **ownership** of the house should be in the name of the **female head** of the household or in **joint names**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)**: Launched in **May 2016** from **Ballia, Uttar Pradesh**, this scheme focuses on providing **clean cooking fuel (LPG)** to women from **Below Poverty Line (BPL)** households to replace unhealthy traditional fuels like wood and coal. *Hence, option 2 is incorrect.*

• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**: This is a **National Mission for Financial Inclusion** launched on **28th August 2014**. It aims to provide universal access to **banking facilities**, including **savings accounts, insurance, and pensions**, ensuring that every household has at least one bank account. *Hence, option 3 is incorrect.*

• **Skill India Mission**: Launched on **15th July 2015**, this initiative aims to train over **40 crore people** in India in different skills by **2022**. It includes the **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)** to enhance the **employability** of the Indian youth. *Hence, option 4 is incorrect.*

• **Digital India**: A campaign launched in **2015** to ensure that **government services** are made available to citizens electronically by improving **online infrastructure** and increasing **Internet connectivity**.

• **Saubhagya Scheme**: Also known as **Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana**, it was launched in **September 2017** to achieve **universal household electrification** in the country.

**Important Points__**

• **Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS)**: Under **PMAY-Urban**, beneficiaries from **EWS, LIG, and MIG** categories can avail of an **interest subsidy** of up to **6.5%** on home loans for a tenure of **20 years**.

• **Beneficiary Identification**: For the **PMAY-Gramin** component, the selection of beneficiaries is done based on the **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011** data, which ensures transparency and reaches the most **vulnerable sections**.

• **In-situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR)**: This component of **PMAY-U** uses **land as a resource** to provide houses to **slum dwellers** in partnership with private developers.

• **Funding Pattern**: In **PMAY-G**, the cost of the house is shared between the **Central and State Governments** in the ratio of **60:40** in plain areas and **90:10** for **North-Eastern** and **Himalayan States**.

• **Convergence**: The scheme works in convergence with other programs like **Swachh Bharat Mission** for toilets and **MGNREGA** for providing **unskilled labor** wages for house construction.
